Ancient human remains discovered beneath Mexico City railway project reveal possible pre-Hispanic ossuary
description: Archaeologists working along the route of the Mexico City–Querétaro passenger railway have uncovered a possible ancient ossuary containing human remains, ceramics and stone artifacts near the Buenavista terminal, in a discovery that could shed new light on burial practices during one of the most transformative periods in Mexican history. The discovery, announced by Mexico's National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH), includes nine sets of human skeletal remains, five mandibles and a variety of other bones, some of which show evidence of intentional cranial modification. Associated objects suggest that the deposit may date to the Late Postclassic period (1200–1519 CE) or the early years of contact between Indigenous communities and Spanish conquerors (1519–1535 CE).
